chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Columbia, Missouri: high school parties and the John Dillinger band
summary: In Columbia, Missouri, he led a high school band called the John Dillinger band, mused about the word jazz, and had given up the violin for piano.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And he was not a straightjacket sort of person. He had an appreciation for humor as well as strict ways, you know. But as I said then we lived in places -- I lived in Columbia, Missouri, where I went to high school. And I might even go to that part of my life because this is going into my junior high school age, which I remember the next step of my life that I remember -- would remember things of significance.
And it was when we were living in Columbia, Missouri. My pronunciation is terrible today. This is unfortunate, I can't get my lips to working.

But I remember as I said going to these different schools, but my next vivid thoughts were when I went to school in Columbia, Missouri, then it was that I had become quite mature in my mind, and I was playing music for parties in my junior high school year, up until the time I was a junior in high school, ready to graduate from high school. And it was during this time that I really remember playing for these parties, and would you believe it we had a band, I had a band, and for some reason or other I called it the John Dillinger band. Now I don't know why -- this is just how young people were in those days. You know, you pick out some name, out of something -- I don't know, show business has always been a crazy thing. And pick out some name or something and say what are you going to call this? Oh, call it -- like the word jazz, in fact, I think came about by some accident. What are they playing? Oh, some jazz. You know, that jazzy stuff, jazzy stuff, you fellas, you know.
And there's a saying also that, you know, if you play some music and it's not absolutely correct, and not just perfect, they'll say well that's good enough for
jazz, as if jazz music is not supposed to be right. You know. Yes, yes.

But this name meant nothing entirely except as a publicity stunt; really, in those days, as a high school boy playing for the parties. I played for the high school parties with my band, which probably included a bass and drums and piano most of the time, and perhaps some young musician played the sax or trumpet, I don't even remember.
You were playing piano, not violin.
Piano. Oh, no, no. I had stopped the violin now by this time --

Because as I said, the inspiration for the violin had diminished, and I enjoyed playing the piano more and the piano was right there, and I first fell in love with the piano. And it just seemed to be the instrument for me at the time.
